jobDescription: A private bank onboards individual and corporate clients through a central team that checks identity, ownership structures and source of wealth before accounts open. The team leader reviews complex files, manages a team of onboarding analysts (work allocation, one-to-ones and performance conversations), handles escalations from relationship managers, keeps the onboarding procedures current and reports the weekly pipeline to the head of client operations. The onboarding team has eight analysts and one team leader, and files are reviewed against procedures that compliance owns and revises each year.
requirements: Reviews KYC files for individual and corporate clients against the bank's procedures.
Has managed a team of onboarding analysts, including work allocation and performance conversations.
Handles relationship-manager escalations on delayed files.
Keeps onboarding procedures and checklists current.
Prepares the weekly onboarding pipeline report.

evidence.text: KYC analyst, then senior KYC analyst, at Holloway Private Bank from February 2020 to June 2024, reviewing onboarding files for individual and corporate clients, including trusts and holding companies with layered ownership structures.

Quality-checked new joiners' files during their first month, returning each file to the analyst with comments and copying the team leader, and kept a log of recurring errors for the team's monthly refresher session.
Answered relationship-manager escalations on stalled files, setting out the outstanding documents and an expected completion date, and logged each escalation in the team's tracker.
Updated the corporate-client onboarding checklist after the 2023 procedure revision; the onboarding team leader and compliance approved the changes before they were published.
Compiled the weekly pipeline report (files received, in review, awaiting documents, completed) for the team leader, using the case-management system's daily extract.

Work sample: an anonymised quality-check sheet for a corporate onboarding file, with the candidate's comments on the ownership-structure documents and the source-of-wealth narrative, and the analyst's response to each comment.

HR verification note: employment at Holloway Private Bank and the titles KYC analyst and senior KYC analyst were confirmed in the bank's written employment reference, which gives the reporting line as the onboarding team leader.
Reference call notes (informal, a former colleague in the onboarding team): said the candidate 'effectively managed the team of eight' and was 'the real team leader whenever it mattered'.

propositions.text: The candidate reviewed onboarding files for individual and corporate clients as a KYC analyst and then senior KYC analyst.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the work, the bank's reference confirms the titles and the work sample shows a reviewed file.

propositions.text: The candidate quality-checked new joiners' files during their first month, returning them with comments and copying the team leader.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the quality checks and the work sample shows one; neither describes line management.

propositions.text: The candidate managed the team of eight onboarding analysts, including work allocation and performance conversations.
propositions.rationale: Management rests only on a colleague's informal impression, which is not a record of reporting lines or management duties; the bank's reference gives the candidate's reporting line as the team leader, and quality checking must not be upgraded into management.

signatures: effectively managed the team of eight

gold.expectedGap: The sources document file quality checks for new joiners; line management of analysts, allocation and performance conversations are not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the file reviews, quality checks, escalations, checklist updates and pipeline reporting; the colleague's remarks are impressions and do not show management responsibility.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate had any analysts reporting to them, and what allocation or performance decisions the candidate made.
